tagline: A winding county road links hamlets through a succession of right-angle turns.
intro: The Trail is Route 14’s winding run southeast from US 360 at St. Stephens Church through King and Queen County. Multiple right-angle turns shape the drive along the county’s main north–south highway. It passes hamlets and the county seat before meeting Route 33 at Shacklefords.

The Route 14 number once continued northwest beyond St. Stephens Church toward Bowling Green; that older alignment is now Route 721, Newtown Road. The numbered highway now starts at US 360 and connects the county seats of King and Queen, Gloucester and Mathews counties.

From St. Stephens Church, follow The Trail southeast through Bruington and Stevensville to King and Queen Court House. The county seat lies on the north side of the Mattaponi River valley. Beyond it come Little Plymouth, Shanghai and Elsom, then the junction with Route 33 at Shacklefords.

moments.title: Stevensville
moments.text: Stevensville is an agricultural community along Route 14, east of Bruington and St. Stephens Church. Near Stevensville, the junction of Routes 631 and 632 has been known as Dahlgrens Corner since at least 1918. The name recalls Union colonel Ulric Dahlgren, killed in King and Queen County in March 1864 after his force failed to penetrate Richmond’s defenses. Confederate cavalry and Home Guards ambushed his group near Walkerton; most survivors were captured. Papers found on his body allegedly ordered Richmond burned and Jefferson Davis and his cabinet assassinated. Their authenticity is disputed; Meade, Kilpatrick and Lincoln disavowed knowledge of them.

moments.title: King and Queen Court House
moments.text: The courthouse compound gathers the court, clerk’s office and county jail within a setting partly defined by a brick wall. The courthouse dates from circa 1750. Union troops burned it on March 10, 1864; it was repaired and remains in service. The village’s government complex includes both old and new courthouses. Another building became a place to preserve county history: renovation of Fary Tavern began in December 1999, and the Courthouse Tavern Museum opened in May 2001. The King and Queen Historical Society operates the museum in partnership with the county as an archive, museum and cultural center.

moments.title: Upper Church, Stratton Major Parish
moments.text: Near Shanghai, Upper Church is a one-story brick rectangle beneath a steeply pitched gable roof. Built between about 1724 and 1729, it was restored after fire gutted the interior in the 1840s. The church has been used by Baptists and later Methodists since the early nineteenth century.
